emily: heads up — while onboarding hf/chat_template->redwood conversion for zikron-13b I hit a weird token mismatch when templates contain Jinja choice blocks. model output quality dropped after quantization. :thinking_face: emily: minimal repro: original template snippet: ```jinja {% set options = ['A','B'] %} User: Pick one: {% for o in options %}- {{ o }} {% endfor %} Assistant: {{ chosen }} ``` emily: when prerendered & converted to Redwood prompt we end up with an extra sentinel for the choice loop like `<|aux_choice|>` injected between list items and the assistant marker, which the tokenizer maps to multiple tokens. leads to different kv-cache offsets and subtle tokenization splits post-quant. jordan: can you paste the rendered output you feed to the runtime? also what tokenizer (hf tokenizer name + vocab) are you using? emily: rendered string we send (sanitized): ``` User: Pick one: - A <|aux_choice|>- B Assistant: <|assistant|> Hello ``` emily: tokenizer: `zikron/tokenizer-v1` (based on byte-level BPE), config.json had `special_tokens_map` with `{\"aux_choice\": \"<|aux_choice|>\"}` that was added during conversion.
quant: int8 dynamic using q8_0 with Triton kernels. sam: quick check — run `python -c "print(tokenizer.encode('A <|aux_choice|>- B'))"` and compare to `print(tokenizer.encode('A - B'))` — if aux token splits, kv-cache positions shift. also run a raw tokenized diff between HF and Redwood tokenizers (if you have both). emily: ran that, aux token becomes 3 tokens on this tokenizer whereas HF expected a single special token. so conversion of `special_tokens_map` didn't update the tokenizer files on the bundle we ship to Dedicated. maria: this sounds like a config-sync bug: in `config.json` we translate HF `special_tokens_map` -> redwood `extra_tokens` but we may have missed updating `tokenizer.json` / merges when converting. also check `role_prefixes` mapping for chat_template -> prompt; if assistant role prefix is appended after aux tokens it will create unexpected sequences. jordan: could also be Jinja whitespace control. If `{%-` or `-%}` was used, we might be collapsing newlines and the aux token lands next to punctuation and splits differently. can you try with explicit sentinel spacing: `{{ "<|aux_choice|>" }}` vs raw to confirm? emily: good call. tried forcing spaces, spacing changed splitting but still not single token. sam: workaround until tokenizer bundle is fixed: 1) avoid emitting the aux sentinel as a standalone special token; instead emit a plain ASCII marker like `[[choice]]` and map it to a single token at tokenization build step (but requires rebuild) OR 2) post-process rendered prompt to replace aux sentinel with a sequence that tokenizes identically across hf/redwood. neither ideal. maria: long-term fix: update conversion script to ensure special tokens are registered in `tokenizer.json` and `vocab` and add a unit test in eng-ml that asserts `encode(sentinel)` is single token. add an eval that measures generation divergence pre/post quant on sample chat flows that use choice blocks. emily: FYI CI caught a regression in canary: deploy-bot reported a quality drop on `conversational-choice-suite` after quant rollout. @eng-ml — I'm opening a short P0 triage to sync with runtime and infra to get a tokenizer bundle patch out. deploy-bot: CI: canary-quality-check failed (conversational-choice-suite) — regression delta 0.12 BLEU-style metric. https://ci.redwood.example/builds/4234 jordan: thanks, I can pair on the tokenizer bundle. if we patch quickly we should revert the quant rollout for zikron-13b on Dedicated to avoid customer impact. emily: negatives: customers with choice-heavy prompts see hallucination + trailing garbage token in outputs post-quant. positives: repro is small and deterministic. maria: assigning to @sam for bundle, @jordan for rollback plan, @emily for triage doc. please drop short notes in #eng-oncall if we flip traffic. emily: will do, I'll paste the triage doc + minimal test into this thread in a bit. :thumbsup:
